questions.q: By default, what happens when one row out of millions fails a data type conversion in a data flow component?
options: The entire Data Flow task fails — no rows load, even the good ones
SSIS silently skips just that one row and continues
The row is automatically written to a default error log file
The component retries the row up to three times before continuing
questions.explain: Without an error output configured, most components treat any row-level failure as fatal to the whole component, failing the entire Data Flow task.

questions.q: What is the key difference between an error and a truncation in SSIS?
options: An error is an unrecoverable failure that produces a NULL; a truncation is data cut short but still usable
An error only applies to numeric columns, truncation only to text columns
There is no real difference — SSIS treats them identically
A truncation always crashes the package, but an error never does
questions.explain: SSIS tracks these as two distinct, independently configurable conditions: errors can't produce a usable result at all, while truncations produce an incomplete but usable one.

questions.q: Which of the three error/truncation dispositions actually redirects the failed row to a separate processing path?
options: Redirect Row
Fail Component
Ignore Failure
Retry Row
questions.explain: Redirect Row sends the failed row down the component's error output; Fail Component stops the task, and Ignore Failure lets the row continue down the normal output unchanged.

questions.q: What two columns does SSIS automatically add to a component's error output?
options: ErrorCode and ErrorColumn
ErrorMessage and ErrorTimestamp
RowNumber and TableName
SourceName and Severity
questions.explain: ErrorCode identifies what went wrong numerically, and ErrorColumn identifies which column caused it — GetErrorDescription() can turn the code into readable text.

questions.q: Why might you connect a component's error output to a Script Component before writing rows to an error file?
options: To call GetErrorDescription() on the ErrorCode and turn it into a readable message before it's logged
Script Components are required by SSIS before any error output can be used
To automatically retry the failed row a second time
To convert the error output into the component's normal (green) output
questions.explain: ErrorCode and ErrorColumn alone aren't very readable — a Script Component calling GetErrorDescription() against the ComponentMetaData turns the numeric code into an actual description.
